correctness.rationale: On H^2 the monomial actions send an input e_{p*l} into the unique output e_{q*l}, giving disjoint singular columns. For d=gcd(m,n), d∤l gives weight r^((p+q)l), and l=dh gives the exact difference r^(Lh)*(b^m conjugate(a)^n)^h-r^(2h)*(b conjugate(a))^h. Summing absolute weights yields the stated geometric component plus the e^(-2u) Haar-phase Riemann integral. The orbit xi^h is periodic or equidistributed, with exponentially summable tails; strictly greater averages for any nontrivial phase group give R(xi)>R(1). Squaring and summing gives the three-term Hilbert–Schmidt identity and the resonance-only leading cross term. Basiswise strong convergence follows by uniform boundedness; compactness of each r<1 approximant excludes operator-norm convergence to noncompact K_1, and d=1,xi=1 has a positive max e^(-2u)-e^(-Lu) defect. Hypotheses m,n>=2, fixed unit phases and common r are used. The finite check.py constructs matrix columns and bounded sums, not infinite-limit certificates.
